checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, flat, and bright yellow, matching the description for a mallard drake.
The eye is visible on the side of the green head and appears dark/black.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is consistent with a swimming duck, appearing streamlined and floating correctly on the water surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, brown chest, and grey/brown flanks.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: One orange leg/foot is visible underwater. It shows the correct anatomical position (set back) and the visible portion suggests webbing typical of waterfowl.
The folded wing is visible on the side of the body, showing proper feather layering and structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible at the rear, appearing short and slightly upturned, consistent with a drake.
